decision.rationale: The 48-file package is hash-consistent, both validator modes pass, the full declared matrix executes, R3 through R6 remain closed for their stated counterexamples, and R7 now enforces cardinality, canonical ordering, full tuple and authority binding, unique immutable requests, provider-resource and CAS equality, receipt and tombstone row order, raw key equality, and zero-effect denial for its declared negative cases. Two independently executable gaps remain. First, arbitrary unique SHA-256-looking strings can stand in for provider receipts because the lifecycle input carries no provider-receipt evidence objects and the oracle validates only the signed disposition record's digest assertions; it can therefore claim deleted-tombstoned without evidence that any provider performed the destructive effect. Second, an exact same-key and same-bytes retry that correctly returns REPLAY_NOOP from the protected-action oracle is converted by lifecycleDecision into LIFECYCLE_REPLAY_NOOP blocked state even when complete matching receipt and tombstone evidence exists, so crash recovery cannot converge idempotently. Zero technical blocker or major is not met, so the candidate is not ready for authorized incorporation.

newFindings.title: Unbacked provider-receipt digests can prove destructive lifecycle completion

observedCase.construction: Start from the valid two-copy RC-FAILED-RUN fixture. Replace the two copyReceipts providerReceiptDigest values with arbitrary unique 64-character values consisting only of a and b, reseal the disposition receipt, bind the new receipt digest and rows into a resealed tombstone, and regenerate the final protected tombstone request so all declared downstream bindings remain coherent. Supply no provider-receipt bytes, schemas, signatures, stable provider IDs, provider timestamps, or independently verified effect records because lifecycleDecision has no such input.
observedCase.expected: Block with typed zero effects because a digest assertion inside a locally signed disposition record cannot prove that a provider receipt exists, is authentic, identifies the exact request/resource/effect, and records a completed provider outcome.
observedCase.observed: lifecycleDecision returned deleted-tombstoned with firstError null and effects.lifecycle=1. The input had no provider-receipt evidence fields and accepted the arbitrary a and b digests.

newFindings.impact: A lifecycle worker or compromised local signer can fabricate unique digest strings, assert deleted or crypto-erased effects, and obtain a durable tombstone without presenting or verifying the provider evidence. The oracle therefore does not prove that every copy was deleted or every raw key was erased, so false completion can hide retained personal data or failed irreversible operations.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Define and hash-bind a canonical provider disposition-receipt schema or binding-specific schemas. Require one independently authentic provider receipt object per ordered present tuple, supplied as immutable bytes and verified for provider identity, stable provider request and resource IDs, exact immutable request digest or idempotency key, tenant and full copy or key tuple, effect and terminal provider state, server timestamp after the authorized request and before the aggregate disposition receipt, and current provider proof or independently archived evidence. Compute providerReceiptDigest from those verified bytes, require a one-to-one ordered mapping with no missing, duplicate, extra, substituted, stale, partial, unknown, wrong-tenant, wrong-resource, wrong-effect, or replayed receipt, and block with typed zero effects before tombstone authorization when any check fails. Add passing two-copy and raw-multikey provider-receipt cases plus coherent resealed arbitrary-digest and every binding-negative case. Refresh all affected hashes and repeat fresh independent pre-incorporation review.

newFindings.title: Exact idempotent lifecycle retries cannot converge from REPLAY_NOOP

observedCase.construction: Start from the valid two-copy RC-FAILED-RUN fixture with complete matching receipt and tombstone evidence. For both provider actions and the final tombstone action, change the signed authoritative replay-ledger snapshot from unused to committed and set requestDigest to that action's unchanged immutable request digest. Preserve every selector, idempotency key, resource snapshot, CAS snapshot, receipt row, and tombstone row.
observedCase.expected: Treat each protected-action REPLAY_NOOP as successful prior completion with no duplicate provider effect, verify the already completed receipt and tombstone, and converge to deleted-tombstoned with no new destructive effect.
observedCase.observed: protectedActionDecision's specified same-key and same-bytes condition became REPLAY_NOOP, but lifecycleDecision rejected every non-ALLOW result and returned blocked with LIFECYCLE_REPLAY_NOOP and all-zero effects.

newFindings.impact: A normal crash or acknowledgement loss after a committed provider effect can leave lifecycle reconciliation permanently blocked even though the exact immutable request, provider receipt, and tombstone are present. Raw erasure and ordinary deletion cannot reliably resume without inventing a new idempotency key or request, which would conflict with the no-duplicate-effect contract.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Define lifecycle-specific handling for protected-action REPLAY_NOOP. Accept it only when the authoritative replay ledger proves the same idempotency key and exact immutable request digest were committed, the independently verified provider receipt proves the corresponding exact effect, and the receipt or tombstone chain is complete and temporally coherent. A same-key different-bytes replay, missing or mismatched receipt, uncommitted state, stale snapshot, CAS mismatch, partial provider outcome, or duplicated effect must still block with typed zero effects. Add exact same-bytes retry positives at each provider-copy step and the final tombstone step, including mixed fresh-ALLOW and prior-REPLAY_NOOP recovery after every crash cut, plus drift and duplicate-effect negatives. Refresh all affected hashes and repeat fresh independent pre-incorporation review.
